gaps: Cosplay-specific professional teaching on dynamic still portraits, movement cues, costume/hair/weapon interaction, and convention-floor constraints remains sparse.
Need deeper primary-source coverage of a simple single-person shot: define start, action/process and end; coordinate subject path, camera path, framing and focus in a short clip.
Need more professional portrait sources distinguishing intentional camera motion from subject motion and camera shake.

Continuity is represented mainly by curriculum and case studies; seek authoritative editor/director/DP instruction on matching screen direction, eyelines, prop/action state, and coverage at beginner scale.
No Chinese primary cinematographer material or Japanese primary cinematography teaching was opened; Japanese still-photo motion sources were opened.
Manual-focus pulling in moving cosplay portraits remains under-triangulated at professional entry level; available practical detail is from a museum curriculum plus cinema case studies.
